scenes.say: In eight days in July 1969, humans flew to the Moon and back. Here is how it happened, day by day.
July sixteenth. Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins blast off from Florida on a giant Saturn Five rocket.
July nineteenth. After three days and almost four hundred thousand kilometres, they reach the Moon.
scenes.sub: from the Earth to the Moon

scenes.say: July twentieth. Alarms are going off and fuel is running out, so Armstrong flies the lander by hand. The Eagle has landed.
scenes.sub: landed with under a minute of fuel

scenes.say: That night, around six hundred million people watch Armstrong take the first step on the Moon.
They plant a flag, collect rocks, and spend about two and a half hours walking on another world.
July twenty first. The Eagle lifts off and rejoins Michael Collins, who has been orbiting the Moon alone.
July twenty fourth. The capsule splashes down in the Pacific Ocean. Mission accomplished.
And their footprints are still up there today, because the Moon has no wind to blow them away.
